title: Agents will shop for shoppers, so our store must be agent-ready by holiday
summary: 55% of consumers use AI in product discovery (NIQ); Gartner: 34% would use GenAI for gift ideas. Target built its holiday plan on an AI assistant; Walmart opened to outside agents. PC shipments fell 21% in Q3 (Counterpoint).

points.headline: Retailers are setting the rules for AI shopping agents
points.detail: Walmart added spending controls and agent profiles for outside agents while Amazon blocks them; Target built its holiday plan on an AI assistant. We must decide how agents may read and buy from our store.

points.headline: AI is now a mainstream discovery channel for shoppers
points.detail: NIQ finds 55% of consumers use AI in discovery; Gartner says 34% of US consumers would use GenAI for holiday gifts. Our product content and data must work for AI tools.

points.headline: PC demand is collapsing while memory costs push prices up
points.detail: Counterpoint: PC shipments fell 21% in Q3, Q4 forecast to fall 27%, with a memory shortage driving record price inflation. We should plan promotions, pricing and inventory for a weak Q4.

points.headline: Holiday budgets tighten even as online sales grow
points.detail: Gartner: nearly 60% of US consumers have less to spend this holiday, while Adobe forecasts record $275.1B online sales. We should lean on value, financing and deal depth.

points.headline: Best Buy adds TikTok Shop as channels multiply
points.detail: Best Buy joined TikTok Shop for its biggest holiday season yet, giving electronics shoppers a new route to purchase. We should test our own presence and promotions there.
